video_title: Are Markets About to Take Off Again? w/ Andreas Steno & Mikkel Rosenvold | Macro Mondays
gist: Note: despite the title billing Raoul Pal, this episode is hosted by Mikkel Rosenvold with guest Andreas Steno (Macro Mondays); Raoul Pal does not appear in the transcript. Steno and Rosenvold argue the crypto rally is a continuation of the short-dollar/debasement trade fueled by Bessent's bond buybacks, see exhausted bearish positioning (44% net-long oil, bearish AAII) setting up a Q4 rally, and flag a resurgent South Korea-led semiconductor cycle (exports +80% YoY) alongside a constructive Trump-Xi summit backdrop.

themes.theme: AI and crypto: convergence, not rotation

insights.claim: AI and crypto are not competing trades where money rotates from one to the other; Andreas Steno argues they work in tandem over time and rejects the popular narrative that being long AI means you must pivot into the crypto rally.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: Investors framing 2025-26 as an AI-vs-crypto rotation trade may be using the wrong mental model; Steno's view argues for holding both rather than switching.
insights.quote: I think it's a wrong question whether it's either or. It's AI and crypto in tandem over time.

insights.claim: Crypto is positioned as the transaction rail for an emerging AI agent economy because traditional fiat rails cannot efficiently support agent-to-agent microtransactions, and early evidence of this is appearing with SUI reportedly being used for agent-to-agent transactions amid a rapid rise in the number of live AI agents since roughly mid-May/early-June.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: If agent-to-agent commerce scales, blockchain-based payment rails could see structural (not just speculative) demand -- a thesis to track via on-chain agent-transaction volume rather than price alone.
insights.quote: we begin to see stories of especially SUI being used for inter AI or agentto agent transactions.

themes.theme: Dollar debasement and crypto rally mechanics

insights.claim: The current crypto rally is best explained as an extension of a broader short-dollar proxy trade that has been running since July, rather than a fresh, independent catalyst.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: Treat crypto strength as correlated with dollar-debasement/short-dollar positioning broadly, meaning a dollar reversal or unwind of that macro trade could pressure crypto even without crypto-specific news.
insights.quote: short dollar proxy trade that we've had on since July

insights.claim: The original catalyst that revived the crypto/reflation narrative was Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent acknowledging the long end of the yield curve was slightly out of control and then ramping up the pace of Treasury bond buyback operations, which reignited a broader fiscal-debasement narrative tied to US debt levels.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: Watch Treasury buyback cadence and long-end yield behavior as a leading indicator/trigger for renewed debasement-trade flows into gold, Bitcoin and crypto.
insights.quote: started by Scott Besson's buyback operations that suddenly revived the whole narrative and the whole momentum of the space.

insights.claim: This crypto rally looks more fundamentally healthy than a purely policy-driven move because it is happening even though Congress failed to pass the CLARITY Act, meaning it is not a government-bailout-style rally, and it coincides with early signs of blockchains being used for actual agent-driven transactions.
insights.speaker: Mikkel Rosenvold
insights.so_what: A rally not dependent on favorable legislation may be more durable than a pure regulatory-catalyst trade; regulatory setbacks (like a stalled CLARITY Act) may matter less than assumed.
insights.quote: cryptos rallying so this is not some government bailout driven rally

themes.theme: Crowded positioning and the setup for Q4

insights.claim: Speculative futures positioning in oil is net 44% long as a share of open interest, a very crowded long that has built up over the recent oil/Iran-driven rally.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: A crowded 44% net-long in oil raises the risk of a sharp unwind/pullback if de-escalation headlines continue, independent of fundamentals.
insights.quote: the market is net 44% long in oil of the open market interest in futures.

insights.claim: Markets failing to move further in the 'expected' direction after a hawkish Fed message and a hotter-than-expected core CPI print, combined with extremely bearish AAII retail-investor sentiment despite an unresolved Ukraine-Russia conflict, is read as a symptom of exhausted, one-sided positioning rather than genuine fundamental weakness.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: When bad news stops moving markets in the 'obvious' direction, treat it as a positioning-exhaustion signal and a potential contrarian buy setup rather than confirmation of the bearish narrative.
insights.quote: that is to me a symptom of a market that has a very exhausted positioning already.

insights.claim: Steno expects the seasonal 'September phobia' bearish narrative to fade into a Q4 rally, similar to last year when extreme September bearishness (especially around momentum names) preceded a large rally; he separately flags that a future round of global central-bank rate hikes could eventually cap the business cycle, but views that risk as a 2027 story, not an immediate one.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: Positions for a Q4 relief rally (particularly in momentum/growth names) while flagging 2027 central-bank tightening as the theme to monitor for when the cycle risk resurfaces.
insights.quote: There's money to be made in that interum there.

themes.theme: Semiconductor cycle and South Korea trade data

insights.claim: South Korea's preliminary trade data for the first 20 days of the month showed export growth accelerating to almost 80% year-over-year (even higher when adjusted for working days), with semiconductor exports specifically up around 250% year-over-year and broader ex-semiconductor exports up roughly 20-22% year-over-year.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: South Korea's export data is a real-time, high-frequency read on global tech demand; the +250% YoY semiconductor print argues the AI/semi capex cycle is still accelerating, not decelerating.
insights.quote: semis are up 250% year-over-year something like that it's absolutely bizarre

insights.claim: South Korean trade data is one of the earliest available gauges of global economic-cycle health, and its continued acceleration -- despite Fed hikes, an oil-price shock, and ongoing geopolitical wars -- indicates the global business cycle is not rolling over yet.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: Use South Korea trade releases as an early-warning/confirmation indicator for the global cycle rather than waiting on lagging US data.

insights.claim: The rebound in NASDAQ and semiconductor stocks on this data reflects that the market was simply not positioned for continued acceleration, after weeks of bearish positioning that Steno argues was not grounded in fundamentals; he still concedes 2027 could turn out weak but says it is too early to call the cycle dead.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: Fade extreme bearish positioning in semis/NASDAQ when hard data (like Korea exports) keeps beating it; but keep 2027 on the radar as a genuine cycle risk rather than dismissing it outright.

themes.theme: Geopolitics: US-China summit, Iran, and Greenland

insights.claim: Ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, US officials reportedly hold sympathy for new semiconductor tariffs and for banning more chip-making equipment exports to China, which could also prevent renewal of Chinese operating licenses for Korean semiconductor companies -- but Steno does not expect a major trade-war escalation at the summit given conciliatory signals over the weekend.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: Watch Korean semiconductor/memory names for headline risk around China-license renewal decisions tied to the summit, even as broad trade-war escalation risk looks lower than a few weeks ago.
insights.quote: it would be a major surprise to see some sort of big escalation towards the end of the week

insights.claim: The US and China have become less focused on escalating their trade war against each other partly because both are now facing high energy costs stemming from the Iran conflict and have a shared incentive to coordinate so energy prices don't spiral further.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: A shared energy-cost pain point between the US and China is an underappreciated de-escalation force for the trade relationship, separate from the AI-policy common ground being reported.
insights.quote: even foes they can find common ground when they have something they need to solve together

insights.claim: The new US-Greenland deal should be understood as a hedge against a small but potentially catastrophic tail risk (an independent Greenland aligning with China or Russia) rather than as a full resolution of underlying tensions -- akin to a hedge fund paying up to mitigate a low-probability, high-impact scenario.
insights.speaker: Mikkel Rosenvold
insights.so_what: Frame geopolitical 'deals' like this as tail-risk mitigation rather than resolution; residual friction (e.g., over how each side represents the deal) can persist even after signing.
insights.quote: It's potentially one that could trigger a world war.

insights.claim: Steno reads the Iran conflict as moving in cyclical 'sine waves' of escalation and de-escalation and believes the region is currently past peak escalation, consistent with his earlier (and admittedly early) April call that the conflict was effectively over.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: If the sine-wave de-escalation pattern holds, oil's geopolitical risk premium likely continues to fade, reinforcing the case for unwinding crowded long-oil positioning.
insights.quote: my reading of the conflict in the Middle East is that it moves in sine waves

themes.theme: Portfolio construction: long gold, crypto and semis together

insights.claim: In Steno's/Real Vision's macro portfolio, the crypto sleeve has outperformed precious metals (gold) by more than their own machine-learned nowcasting model expected, which was itself a surprise to Steno.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: Even systematic/quant signals underestimated crypto's relative strength versus gold in this cycle, suggesting the debasement trade is rotating more aggressively into crypto than models assumed.
insights.quote: it's been a bit of a surprise to see uh the crypto sleeve outperform precious metals to the extent that we've seen.

insights.claim: Steno's portfolio is directionally long all three of gold, crypto (including Bitcoin), and AI/semiconductors simultaneously, reflecting a base case that all three grind higher into Q4 rather than favoring a rotation between them.
insights.speaker: Andreas Steno
insights.so_what: A barbell of debasement hedges (gold, crypto) plus a growth/AI-capex trade (semis) is Steno's preferred Q4 setup rather than picking a single winner.
insights.quote: we're basically long all three, meaning that we directionally think all three will go up here.
